title: the Yaksha's questions
hook: one by one the brothers go to the lake, each with his own strength, and each ignores the voice
carry: the lake wants to be answered

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Yaksha's questions began with a stolen pair of fire-sticks, and Nakula drank before he listened. Your line was a brother who didn't wait to hear them. Did you stop and ask yourself a question before that first drink of water? Day eight hundred two.

Nakula doesn't come back. Under the tree, his brothers wait, and wait, and Yudhishthira sends the next one. Sahadeva, go and find your brother, and bring water. So Sahadeva follows the cranes to the lake. And there is Nakula, lying on the bank. Sahadeva is grieving, and he is burning with thirst, and the voice speaks again, the same words. This lake is mine. Answer first. Back under the tree, three brothers are still waiting for water.
screen: `NAKULA DOESN'T COME BACK.` → `SAHADEVA GOES NEXT.` → `THE SAME VOICE, THE SAME WORDS.`

segments.voice: Sahadeva drinks, and falls beside his brother. Now Yudhishthira sends Arjuna, the great archer. Arjuna reaches the lake with his bow ready, and sees both twins dead. He looks around for an enemy and sees no one. When the voice speaks, Arjuna does what a warrior does. He shoots at it. He sends arrows toward the sound, aiming by ear alone. The voice answers, unhurt: your arrows can't touch me. Answer my questions, and then drink. Arjuna drinks, and falls. Then Bhima comes, the strong one. He sees three brothers on the ground and decides this must be the work of some spirit, and that he'll fight whoever it is. But first, water. The voice warns him too. He doesn't listen. He drinks, and falls. Notice what each one brings. Nakula brings his thirst. Sahadeva brings his grief. Arjuna brings an archer's perfect aim. Bhima brings his strength, and a plan to fight. And not one of them brings what the voice asked for: a moment to listen, and an answer. The lake doesn't want to be conquered. It wants to be answered. Each brother meets it with his own best gift, and for this lake it's the wrong gift. That's the story's warning. Four heroes of the Mahabharata lie on a lakeshore because they wouldn't stop to hear a question. One brother is left.
screen: `SAHADEVA DRINKS, AND FALLS.` · `ARJUNA SHOOTS AT THE VOICE.` · `BHIMA PLANS TO FIGHT, BUT DRINKS.` · then, large: `IT WANTS TO BE ANSWERED.`

segments.voice: Settle, and close your eyes if you like. Let the sounds around you arrive: traffic, a fan, a voice in another room, your own breath. Notice how quickly the mind wants to aim at each one, name it, judge it, do something about it. Don't. Just let each sound come, and go, unanswered and unshot. Breathe in, and hear. Breathe out, and let the sound pass. If you pray, you can rest in that listening as a kind of prayer. The bell holds the time.
Yaksha, the unseen spirit who owns the lake and asks a question before anyone may drink. Four brothers bring thirst, grief, aim and strength, and none of them stops to listen. Today's word.
Your line: the lake wants to be answered. Today, when something pushes back at you, ask what it actually wants before you push harder. Day eight hundred two.

howItsDone: In the epic, the four brothers fall one by one before Yudhishthira arrives, each warned by the same voice in the same words.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. two brothers lie dead by a lake, and an unseen voice says answer first. what do you do?
options: call out and ask the voice its questions.
run back and warn the others.
fork.reveal: he shoots at the voice by sound alone. it is not touched, and it asks him again to answer first. he drinks, and falls.

original.note: Sanskrit: yaksha, a powerful spirit; here the unseen owner of the lake.

trapdoor: what you thought: the brothers were ambushed.
what it means: each was warned, each brought his own strength, and each drank without answering.
what a scholar hears: the scene is built as a series, one brother after another meeting the same words, so that Yudhishthira's arrival lands differently.
recall: bites Nala and changes his shape

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the episode of the Yaksha's questions: Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima at the lake

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli the order Sahadeva, Arjuna, Bhima; Arjuna shooting toward the sound and the voice's reply that his arrows cannot harm it; Bhima's thought that this is the work of yakshas or rakshasas and his intent to fight after drinking.
Superlatives about Arjuna and Bhima removed under the claims rule.
Editor pass: cut 'quiet joke' (flip with four brothers dead) and the templated 'Today, ...' hook closer; howItsDone no longer makes claims about retellings and teachers.
Audit: the review asked 'did you pause before reaching?', which was day 801's old carry before it was replaced; it now picks up 801's actual carry (a question before the first drink of water).
